newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey sell-off agency sees $5.9 bln 1997 revenue.
newsitem.headline: Turkey sell-off agency sees $5.9 bln 1997 revenue.

text.p: Turkey's privatisation agency targets sell-off revenues of $5.9 billion in 1997, well below government forecasts but sharply above actual income raised in past years, state-run Anatolian news agency said on Sunday.

Alongside the $3.3 billion expected to be made from the partial privatisation of Turk Telekom and $1 billion from the sale of a mobile phone service licence, further income of $1.6 billion is anticipated from other sell-offs.

Among companies slated for partial or total sale by Turkey's Privatisation Administration (OIB) are the airline Turk Hava Yollari, petrochemicals firm Petkim, petroleum distributor Petrol Ofisi and oil refiner Tupras.
The revenue forecast follows Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's announcement on Thursday that the government's earlier target for 1997 privatisation revenues would be doubled to $13 billion.
A government spokesman subsequently said $7 billion of this total would come from leasing several hydraulic and thermal power plants next year.

The country's ten-year old privatisation programme has been stalled repeatedly by political opposition and legal obstacles. Turkey has raised some $3 billion through sell-offs since the programme started in 1986.

Sell-off revenues have in the past fallen far short of government forecasts, but the Islamist-led coalition under Erbakan has said privatisation is a priority in its aim to raise badly-needed revenues.
